key_insight: Explainable deep reinforcement learning can optimize residential building energy management while making battery-control decisions understandable to operators.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports lower electricity costs and more reliable operation in PV-battery-equipped buildings by combining forecasting, control, and post-hoc explainability.
method: Trained and compared on-policy and off-policy DRL agents for building energy control.
Used an expanded state space with demand, PV output, battery status, electricity price, weather, and calendar/holiday signals.
Applied post-hoc interpretation methods to explain learned policies and decision behavior.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports evaluation on both synthetic data and real-world Living Lab Energy Campus data, with A2C and PPO achieving the best cumulative rewards and policy stability.
watch_item: Results are shown for one building-management setting, so transferability to other sites, tariffs, and hardware configurations should be validated before deployment.
paper_title: Explainable Data-driven Deep Reinforcement Learning Methods for Optimal Energy Management in Buildings
